issues.description: Condition reads awkwardly; invert to match the spec language directly.
issues.detail: `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` makes the reader parse a double negative for what is really 'layer without a block.' A helper or comment like `// @layer foo; (no block) is allowed before @import` would save the next maintainer a lookup of the CSS Cascade spec. Minor taste issue, not a blocker.

postcss at-rules either have a `nodes` array (block) or not. `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` is verbose where `!node.nodes` does the same job and matches how the rest of postcss-consuming code in this repo tends to read. Style nit against the surrounding codebase voice.

issues.description: Test covers empty block only; add a non-empty `@layer` block case.
issues.detail: The new test uses `@layer foo {}`. The bug is about layers *with blocks*, and an empty block is the degenerate case. A second fixture with `@layer foo { .a {} }` before `@import` would prove the fix isn't accidentally keying on emptiness. Cheap to add, closes the obvious follow-up bug report.

review.summary: One-line fix to one condition, one matching test, one changeset. This is the shape a patch should have: it does one thing, the diff is readable, and the bug it closes is named. The condition itself is correct — a bare `@layer foo;` declaration is still allowed before `@import` per the cascade spec, and only layer at-rules with blocks should be rejected. Taste nits only: the double-negative reads poorly, `typeof === 'undefined'` is verbose where `!node.nodes` would do, and the test should include a non-empty block to lock the behavior down. ACCEPT with trivial fixup.
